role.en: pious king who built Westminster Abbey

bio.en: The last-but-one Anglo-Saxon king. He built Westminster Abbey, consecrated days before his death; he died childless, and the dispute over his succession led to the Norman Conquest. Canonised in 1161.

role.en: king who married Anne of Kiev, daughter of Yaroslav the Wise

bio.en: He fought rebellious vassals, among them his mother Constance and William of Normandy. His wife Anne, daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, bore his heir, Philip I.

role.en: emperor who deposed three rival popes at the Synod of Sutri

bio.en: The height of Salian power: at the Synod of Sutri in 1046 he removed three rival popes and went on to appoint German pontiffs himself, backing the Cluniac church reform. His favourite residence was the palace at Goslar.

role.en: prince of Kiev twice driven from his capital

bio.en: Eldest son of Yaroslav the Wise; together with his brothers he expanded the Russkaya Pravda law code. After the 1068 uprising and quarrels with his brothers he twice lost Kiev, and fell at the Battle of Nezhatina Niva.

role.en: Duke of Normandy, King of England

bio.en: Norman duke who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and conquered England.

role.en: prince of Kiev, father of Vladimir Monomakh

bio.en: The youngest of Yaroslav the Wise's sons to rule Rus, he married a Byzantine princess of the Monomachos family. According to Monomakh he knew five languages; he ruled Kiev from 1078 until his death.

role.en: polymath

bio.en: Song dynasty polymath who first described the magnetic compass for navigation and theorised about geological change.

role.en: theologian, Archbishop of Canterbury

bio.en: Called the father of scholasticism, with the motto "faith seeking understanding". He devised the ontological argument for God from the very idea of a being than which nothing greater can be conceived.

role.en: poet, mathematician, astronomer

bio.en: Mathematician who devised a precise solar calendar and poet famed for his philosophical quatrains, the Rubaiyat.

role.en: emperor humbled at Canossa in his struggle with the pope

bio.en: Excommunicated by Pope Gregory VII in the Investiture Controversy, he stood penitent for three days outside Canossa castle in January 1077. He later took Rome and installed an antipope, but was overthrown by his own son Henry V in 1105.

role.en: prince of Kiev, participant in the Congress of Liubech

bio.en: Son of Iziaslav I. He took part in the Congress of Liubech in 1097 and, with Monomakh, in victorious campaigns against the Cumans; his death was followed by an uprising in Kiev.

role.en: son of Anne of Kiev, excommunicated for bigamy

bio.en: Became king at seven and reigned for 48 years. He married Bertrade de Montfort, taken from her living husband, was excommunicated and so stayed out of the First Crusade.

role.en: Grand Prince of Kiev

bio.en: Grandson of a Byzantine emperor and the last prince to hold Rus' together; author of the 'Instruction' to his children.

role.en: monk and chronicler

bio.en: Monk of the Kiev Caves Monastery traditionally credited with the Primary Chronicle, the key source on early Rus'.

role.en: the Conqueror's son, killed by an arrow while hunting in the New Forest

bio.en: Son of William the Conqueror, nicknamed Rufus. He quarrelled with the church and Archbishop Anselm and built Westminster Hall; he was killed by an arrow while hunting in the New Forest — accident or murder is still unclear.

role.en: Islamic theologian and philosopher

bio.en: One of Islam's most influential thinkers, who reconciled Sufism with orthodoxy and critiqued Aristotelian philosophy.

role.en: Count of Edessa, first King of Jerusalem

bio.en: A leader of the First Crusade who founded the County of Edessa, the first crusader state. In 1100, after the death of his brother Godfrey of Bouillon, he took the title King of Jerusalem and extended the kingdom to the Red Sea.

role.en: law-giving king who created the Exchequer and the Charter of Liberties

bio.en: Youngest son of William the Conqueror. He issued the Charter of Liberties, created the Exchequer and strengthened royal justice; the loss of his heir in the White Ship in 1120 led to civil war after his death.

role.en: Saxon duke elected by the princes in preference to the Staufer

bio.en: Duke of Saxony, elected king in 1125 instead of Frederick of Staufen, sparking the Welf–Staufer feud. Crowned emperor in Rome in 1133, he campaigned against Roger II of Sicily and died on the way back from Italy.

role.en: last ruler of a united Kievan Rus

bio.en: Eldest son of Vladimir Monomakh. He kept almost all of Rus under Kiev's rule and fought the Cumans and Polotsk; soon after his death in 1132 Rus broke up into independent principalities.

role.en: king who tamed the barons around Paris

bio.en: With Abbot Suger as adviser he subdued the unruly lords of the royal domain and strengthened Capetian power. He married his son to Eleanor of Aquitaine, hoping to gain her vast lands.

role.en: Byzantine princess and historian

bio.en: Daughter of Emperor Alexios I and author of the Alexiad, one of the first histories written by a woman.

role.en: Song dynasty poet

bio.en: China's greatest female poet, a master of ci lyrics on love and loss written amid the Jurchen invasion.

role.en: last Salian, who ended the Investiture Controversy with the Concordat of Worms

bio.en: He overthrew his father Henry IV, seized Pope Paschal II in 1111 to force his imperial coronation, and in 1122 agreed the Concordat of Worms, splitting the secular and spiritual investiture of bishops. Married to Matilda of England, he died childless.

role.en: first Staufer king, unlucky leader in the Second Crusade

bio.en: The first Staufer king, never crowned emperor. In 1147 he led the German army on the Second Crusade, was routed by the Seljuk Turks near Dorylaeum and came home empty-handed after the failed siege of Damascus.

role.en: king of the Anarchy, the civil war with Empress Matilda

bio.en: Grandson of William the Conqueror who seized the throne from Henry I's daughter Matilda. Most of his reign was consumed by civil war — the Anarchy; under the Treaty of Wallingford in 1153 Matilda's son Henry became his heir.

role.en: abbess, mystic and composer

bio.en: Benedictine abbess who recorded her visions, wrote on medicine and nature, and is one of the earliest known composers.

role.en: prince of Rostov-Suzdal, founder of Moscow

bio.en: A son of Monomakh who ruled the Rostov-Suzdal land and founded Yuryev-Polsky, Dmitrov and other towns. Moscow's first mention in the chronicles, in 1147, is tied to his invitation; he twice took Kiev, where he died.

role.en: prince who moved the centre of Rus to Vladimir

bio.en: Son of Yuri Dolgoruky. He made Vladimir his capital, built its Golden Gate, the Dormition Cathedral and the Church of the Intercession on the Nerl, and sacked Kiev in 1169. He was murdered by boyar conspirators at his residence in Bogolyubovo.

role.en: Second Crusade leader and first husband of Eleanor of Aquitaine

bio.en: With Conrad III he led the failed Second Crusade (1147–1149). Divorcing Eleanor in 1152 cost him Aquitaine: she married Henry Plantagenet, the future king of England.

role.en: Holy Roman Emperor

bio.en: Emperor who fought for decades to dominate Italy; he drowned in a river while leading the Third Crusade.

role.en: King of the Khmer Empire

bio.en: Buddhist king under whom the Khmer Empire reached its greatest extent; he built Angkor Thom and the Bayon temple.

role.en: Queen of France and of England

bio.en: Europe's richest heiress, wife of two kings and mother of Richard the Lionheart; a patron of troubadours.

role.en: philosopher, commentator on Aristotle

bio.en: Philosopher and physician from Córdoba whose commentaries on Aristotle reintroduced classical thought to medieval Europe.

role.en: Chinese Neo-Confucian philosopher

bio.en: Built the Neo-Confucian synthesis: the world consists of principle (li) and vital energy (qi), and investigating things leads to moral perfection. His commentaries on the Four Books underpinned China's civil exams for 600 years.

role.en: first Plantagenet, builder of the Angevin Empire and of common law

bio.en: First Plantagenet king and husband of Eleanor of Aquitaine, ruling England and half of France. He laid the foundations of English common law and jury trial; his quarrel with Thomas Becket ended in the archbishop's murder in 1170.

role.en: Sultan of Egypt and Syria

bio.en: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty who retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187, admired even by his enemies for his chivalry.

role.en: philosopher, rabbi and physician

bio.en: The greatest medieval Jewish thinker, author of The Guide for the Perplexed and court physician in Saladin's Egypt.

role.en: first shogun of Japan

bio.en: Victor of the Genpei War who founded the Kamakura shogunate, Japan's first samurai government.

role.en: grand prince under whom Vladimir became the strongest power in Rus

bio.en: Brother of Andrey Bogolyubsky, nicknamed for his many children. Under him the Vladimir-Suzdal principality became the strongest in Rus, and the Cathedral of Saint Demetrius was built in Vladimir.

role.en: King of England, crusader

bio.en: Warrior king who led the Third Crusade against Saladin and spent only months of his reign in England.

role.en: founder of the Mongol Empire

bio.en: Unified the Mongol tribes and launched the conquests that created the largest contiguous land empire in history.

role.en: king who took Normandy from the Plantagenets

bio.en: He seized Normandy, Anjou and Maine from King John and in 1214 defeated the coalition of Emperor Otto IV at Bouvines. He joined the Third Crusade; under him Paris was walled and the Louvre begun.

role.en: emperor who held Richard the Lionheart for ransom and won Sicily

bio.en: Barbarossa's son, married to the Sicilian heiress Constance. He extracted a huge ransom for the captive Richard the Lionheart and used it to conquer the Kingdom of Sicily in 1194; he died at Messina aged 32.

role.en: Queen of Georgia

bio.en: The first woman to rule Georgia in her own right; her reign was Georgia's golden age, celebrated by Shota Rustaveli.

role.en: King of England who sealed Magna Carta

bio.en: Youngest son of Henry II. He lost Normandy in 1204, fell out with the pope and the barons, and in 1215 was forced to seal Magna Carta, which limited royal power.

role.en: mathematician

bio.en: Leonardo of Pisa, who introduced Hindu–Arabic numerals to Europe in his Liber Abaci; famous for the sequence named after him.

role.en: Count of Flanders, first Latin Emperor of Constantinople

bio.en: A leader of the Fourth Crusade, which took Constantinople instead of the Holy Land. In 1204 he became the first emperor of the Latin Empire, but a year later he was captured by the Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan at Adrianople and died in captivity.

role.en: the only Welf emperor, beaten by the French at Bouvines

bio.en: Son of Henry the Lion, crowned emperor in 1209. He soon invaded Sicily and was excommunicated by Innocent III, and in 1214, with his English allies, was crushed by Philip II Augustus at Bouvines.

role.en: the first German king to be assassinated

bio.en: Barbarossa's youngest son, elected king in 1198 at the same time as the Welf Otto IV, which set off a decade of civil war. Just as he was winning, he was murdered in Bamberg in 1208 by the count palatine Otto of Wittelsbach.

role.en: saint, founder of the Franciscans

bio.en: A rich merchant's son who renounced wealth for poverty and preaching, and founded the Franciscan order.

role.en: prince who nearly became king of England

bio.en: In 1216, invited by rebel English barons, he landed in England and took London, but withdrew after King John died. As king he led the Albigensian Crusade and died on the way home.

role.en: grand prince of Vladimir killed fighting the Mongols on the Sit

bio.en: Son of Vsevolod the Big Nest and founder of Nizhny Novgorod (1221). During Batu's invasion he lost Vladimir and his family, and was killed at the Battle of the Sit River in March 1238.

role.en: first Russian prince to receive a patent to rule from the Horde

bio.en: Father of Alexander Nevsky. After his brother Yuri's death he rebuilt the land ravaged by the Mongols and in 1243 became the first to receive a patent of rule from Batu; he died returning from Karakorum.

role.en: "Wonder of the World", polyglot emperor who regained Jerusalem without a fight

bio.en: Barbarossa's grandson, raised in Palermo: he spoke several languages, wrote a treatise on falconry and founded the University of Naples (1224). In 1229 he regained Jerusalem by treaty with Sultan al-Kamil, and feuded with the popes all his life.

role.en: Japanese Zen Buddhist teacher

bio.en: Founder of Japanese Soto Zen: enlightenment is not a goal to reach but is expressed in the practice of seated meditation (zazen) itself. Author of the Shōbōgenzō.

role.en: Sultan of Delhi

bio.en: The only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate; she governed in men's attire before being overthrown by the nobility.

role.en: Sufi poet

bio.en: Persian mystic poet, author of the Masnavi; his followers founded the order of whirling dervishes.

role.en: king under whom the English Parliament was born

bio.en: Became king at nine and reigned for 56 years. He rebuilt Westminster Abbey in Gothic style; a barons' revolt led by Simon de Montfort produced the Parliament of 1265, the first to include representatives of the towns.

role.en: crusader king canonised as a saint

bio.en: He led the Seventh and Eighth Crusades, was captured in Egypt and died of disease before Tunis. Famed for his justice, he built the Sainte-Chapelle and was canonised in 1297.

role.en: Great Khan, founder of the Yuan dynasty

bio.en: Grandson of Genghis Khan who conquered southern China and founded the Yuan dynasty; Marco Polo served at his court.

role.en: founder of the Mali Empire

bio.en: The 'Lion King' who defeated the Sosso kingdom and founded the Mali Empire; hero of a West African epic.

role.en: first Habsburg king, who won Austria for his house

bio.en: A Swabian count whose election in 1273 ended the Interregnum. In 1278 he defeated King Ottokar II of Bohemia on the Marchfeld and gave Austria to his sons, making Vienna the Habsburg home for six centuries.

role.en: Prince of Novgorod, Grand Prince

bio.en: Defeated the Swedes on the Neva (1240) and the Livonian Knights on Lake Peipus (1242) while keeping peace with the Horde.

role.en: theologian and philosopher

bio.en: The greatest medieval theologian, who fused Christian doctrine with Aristotle's philosophy in the Summa Theologiae.

role.en: last Staufer to hold the German throne

bio.en: Son of Frederick II, king of Germany, Sicily and Jerusalem, but never emperor. He went to Italy to defend his inheritance against the pope and died of malaria in 1254, after which Germany slid into the Interregnum.

role.en: conqueror of Wales, called the Hammer of the Scots

bio.en: He conquered Wales and ringed it with stone castles, and fought long wars against Scotland, earning the name Hammer of the Scots. He summoned the Model Parliament of 1295 and expelled the Jews from England in 1290.

role.en: king who launched a failed war on Aragon

bio.en: Proclaimed king before Tunis, where his father died. He added the county of Toulouse to the crown and died at Perpignan while retreating from the disastrous Aragonese Crusade.

role.en: minor count deposed by the electors and killed at the Battle of Göllheim

bio.en: A count of Nassau chosen by the electors in 1292 over Rudolf of Habsburg's son because they wanted a weak king. When he tried to build power in Thuringia he was deposed in 1298 and fell fighting Albert of Habsburg at Göllheim.

role.en: Venetian traveller

bio.en: Venetian merchant who spent 17 years in China at Kublai Khan's court; his book opened Asia to European imagination.

role.en: Habsburg king murdered by his own nephew, John the Parricide

bio.en: Son of Rudolf I and duke of Austria, he became king after defeating Adolf of Nassau. He strengthened royal power but in 1308 was murdered by the River Reuss by his disinherited nephew John; Swiss tradition sets the William Tell legend in his reign.

role.en: founder of the Ottoman Empire

bio.en: Leader of a small Anatolian Turkish principality who gave his name to a dynasty and empire lasting over 600 years.

role.en: first prince of Moscow, founder of the Moscow line of the Rurikids

bio.en: Youngest son of Alexander Nevsky, who received the small town of Moscow as his appanage. He annexed Kolomna and Pereslavl-Zalessky and founded the Danilov Monastery; the Russian Church canonised him.

role.en: poet, author of the Divine Comedy

bio.en: Florentine poet whose Divine Comedy, a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise, founded the Italian literary language.

role.en: painter and architect

bio.en: Painter who broke with Byzantine convention, bringing volume and emotion back to art; a forerunner of the Renaissance.

role.en: king who destroyed the Knights Templar

bio.en: He summoned the first Estates General (1302), defeated Pope Boniface VIII and saw the papacy move to Avignon. In 1307 he arrested the Templars and later burned their Grand Master Jacques de Molay.

role.en: Luxembourg emperor on whom Dante pinned his hopes for a revived empire

bio.en: A count of Luxembourg who made his son John king of Bohemia in 1310. He marched into Italy and in 1312 became the first emperor crowned in Rome since Frederick II, but died of malaria near Siena a year later; Dante reserved a throne for him in Paradise.

role.en: ruler of the Mali Empire

bio.en: Malian ruler often called the richest person in history; his gold-laden pilgrimage to Mecca crashed prices in Cairo.

role.en: bey who took Bursa and led the Ottomans into Europe

bio.en: Son of Osman I: took Bursa in 1326 and made it his capital, then captured Nicaea and Nicomedia, and in 1354 seized Gallipoli, the first Ottoman foothold in Europe.

role.en: first Moscow prince to become grand prince of Vladimir

bio.en: Son of Daniel of Moscow and rival of Tver. Having married the sister of Uzbek Khan, he received the patent for the grand principality in 1318; in 1325 he was killed at the Horde by Dmitry of Tver.

role.en: emperor excommunicated by the pope and crowned in Rome without him

bio.en: A Wittelsbach who beat his rival Frederick the Fair at Mühldorf in 1322. Excommunicated by Pope John XXII, he was crowned in Rome by the Roman nobility in 1328, and in 1338 the electors at Rhens declared that their choice needed no papal approval.

role.en: king defeated at Bannockburn and deposed by his wife

bio.en: The first English Prince of Wales. In 1314 he was crushingly defeated by the Scots at Bannockburn; he ruled through favourites, was deposed by his wife Isabella and her lover Mortimer, and was probably murdered at Berkeley Castle.

role.en: English Franciscan philosopher

bio.en: The leading nominalist: universals exist only in the mind and in words, not as things in themselves. His rule against multiplying entities beyond necessity became known as Ockham's razor.

role.en: emperor who overthrew the Kamakura shogunate

bio.en: In 1333, backed by Ashikaga Takauji and Nitta Yoshisada, he overthrew the Kamakura shogunate and tried to rule in person (the Kenmu Restoration). Three years later Takauji drove him from Kyoto; Go-Daigo fled to Yoshino and founded the Southern Court, which rivalled the Northern Court until 1392.

role.en: prince who began the gathering of Russian lands around Moscow

bio.en: He helped the Horde crush the Tver uprising of 1327 and received the patent for the grand principality, along with the right to collect tribute. Under him the metropolitan moved to Moscow, making it the church capital of Rus.

role.en: king whose death led to women being barred from the throne

bio.en: He reigned only a year and a half and reputedly died after drinking cold wine following a ball game. His posthumous son John I lived five days; his brother Philip took the crown and his daughter Joan was passed over.

role.en: prime minister of Majapahit

bio.en: A general and minister who vowed to abstain from 'palapa' until the archipelago was united; under him Majapahit became Southeast Asia's greatest power.

role.en: king who took the throne over his niece

bio.en: Regent for his newborn nephew John I, he had himself crowned after the infant died, and an assembly of notables confirmed that women could not inherit the French crown. He died without sons.

role.en: first Valois king, defeated at Crécy

bio.en: Nephew of Philip IV, made king over the claim of Edward III. The Hundred Years’ War began on his watch: his fleet was destroyed at Sluys (1340), his army at Crécy (1346), Calais fell and the Black Death ravaged the land.

role.en: last king of the senior Capetian line

bio.en: Youngest son of Philip IV; like his brothers, he died without sons. The dispute over his inheritance between Philip of Valois and Edward III of England led to the Hundred Years’ War.
